coverage: Picture this room as a true dining room: a table for four every day and six with guests, chairs that pull out, a sideboard, and the table under the light. The room is also the only way between the kitchen and the living room, so that walk must stay at least 24 inches with the chairs pushed in. Nothing may collide and every chair must be able to pull out. Everything else is a trade-off. Priorities in order: the kitchen-to-living walkway, room behind the chairs, seats, the table under the light, sideboard storage and serving room, rug fit, cost. The TV, sofa and lounge chairs that live here today move to the living room (see tv_room_function).

Polygon / layered furniture and exact circular arc geometry use flatten-js. Ellipses use 192-chord polygons (under 0.006-in radial error at 84 in); boat is an illustrative profile, not manufacturer CAD.
Bounded streamed search retains two fronts per family; not a proof of continuous optimality. Guide bands 24 / 30 / 36 in, chairs 24 hard and 32 / 36 / 44 preference; not code.
The kitchen arch is 97 in jamb-to-jamb but 66.4 in open floor: its north 30.6 in is cabinet. Shared transform dining = nook − (101.1, −54.6) ±2 in.
Unknown base footprint and underside height remain unknown; illustrative models are not stability or knee-room approval. Chair geometry is an overall conservative envelope.
